en: [Uncertain: Our lives are dear to Kolodon,]
uncertainty_note: Opening reads approximately Колодонго ысак жаныбыз; relation and second word unresolved.

en: If we do not bind it to our waists,
uncertainty_note: Object depends on preceding page; conditional is first-person plural, not second-person singular.

en: He himself was the khan of Beijing,
His majesty was lofty, his wrath fierce,
He was a man of exceptional fortune.
Of Kenen among these Kyrgyz,
uncertainty_note: Final case ending on кыргыздан remains slightly uncertain.

en: Of the warrior who vaunts his prowess,
uncertainty_note: Эрдемсиген is a provisional visual reading; final clause belongs with following lines.

en: Of the champion who leads the people,
uncertainty_note: көзөлдүн is likely, but the letter sequence needs specialist review.

en: If we do not attack his assembled people,
uncertainty_note: Opening word tentatively Чогулган; do not regard as secure transcription.

en: [Uncertain: If we do not drive out his petty fury,]
uncertainty_note: Чекене appears written; literal sense of this adjective in the phrase is uncertain.

en: Of the two, Ebegey and Kogoy,
counterpart_note: Secure ordered manuscript/printed counterpart; checked against manuscript image. Orthographic variants retained.

en: Of the heroes Joltoy and Kenen,
counterpart_note: Secure ordered manuscript/printed counterpart; checked against manuscript image. Orthographic variants retained.

en: Of all four, the shelter of their people,
counterpart_note: Secure ordered manuscript/printed counterpart; checked against manuscript image. Orthographic variants retained.

en: If we do not beat their age-old fury out of them,
counterpart_note: Secure ordered manuscript/printed counterpart; checked against manuscript image. Orthographic variants retained.

en: Striking first, before they do,
counterpart_note: Secure ordered manuscript/printed counterpart; checked against manuscript image. Orthographic variants retained.

en: If we do not find some way to deal with them,
counterpart_note: Secure ordered manuscript/printed counterpart; checked against manuscript image. Orthographic variants retained.

en: If we do not block the roads they travel,
counterpart_note: Secure ordered manuscript/printed counterpart; checked against manuscript image. Orthographic variants retained.

en: If we do not drive all their people out,
counterpart_note: Secure ordered manuscript/printed counterpart; checked against manuscript image. Orthographic variants retained.

en: Breaking their hardened backs,
counterpart_note: Secure ordered manuscript/printed counterpart; checked against manuscript image. Orthographic variants retained.

en: Putting their carefree hearts to rest,
uncertainty_note: Manuscript appears көөнүн (contracted көңүлүн), in agreement with printed witness; punctuation editorial.
counterpart_note: Secure ordered manuscript/printed counterpart; checked against manuscript image. Orthographic variants retained.

en: Thrusting spears into their borders,
uncertainty_note: Manuscript clearly includes initial н in найза, unlike printed айза.
counterpart_note: Secure ordered manuscript/printed counterpart; checked against manuscript image. Orthographic variants retained.

en: Destroying those who turn against us,
counterpart_note: Secure ordered manuscript/printed counterpart; checked against manuscript image. Orthographic variants retained.

en: Burning their strongest men,
counterpart_note: Secure ordered manuscript/printed counterpart; checked against manuscript image. Orthographic variants retained.

en: [Uncertain: If we do not test courage in blood,]
uncertainty_note: Tentative reading of both Кайратты and көрбөсөк; final verb could have another vowel.

en: Mighty, exalted True Tengri,
uncertainty_note: Looks Чын Теңир rather than the draft’s personal name Чын Темир. Берен улук and relation to next line remain provisional.

en: If we do not bind him to our waists,
uncertainty_note: Pronoun is provisional from previous line; may mean taking divine power as support.

en: Taking the Muslim people as a whole,
uncertainty_note: бүт кылып is visible; the construction continues into the next lines.

en: [Uncertain: Making their untamed ones into households by the thousand,]
uncertainty_note: A rubbed-out phrase after Азоосун is not recoverable. Remaining words tentatively миңге үй кылып; this translation is conjectural, not a secure reading.

en: [Uncertain: If we do not learn courage through blood.]
uncertainty_note: Кайратты and syntax uncertain; ending билбесек is more likely than draft билбесең.

en: Mecca, upon which they rely,
[Uncertain: When battle begins, striking like lightning,]
uncertainty_note: The middle and final phrase tentatively кирсе чак түшүп; requires review.

en: If we do not drive them as far as Mecca itself,
uncertainty_note: чейин сүрбөсөк is provisional but visually preferable to draft чалып арбасаң.

en: [Uncertain: Extinguishing the fire they rekindled,]
uncertainty_note: First word and noun remain uncertain; best visual reading Жаңгырткан отун өчүрүп.

en: Look among the worthy men,
uncertainty_note: The first word is pale; read provisionally as Жакшылардан.

en: To send the moon coursing from the summer's beginning,
uncertainty_note: Several pale letters in башынан and the final verbal noun require later review.

en: To make the sun smile and send the day coursing,
uncertainty_note: Completion-first reading; the middle and final words are faint.

en: Who struck your people, my child,
His fame spread under the name Kenen,
uncertainty_note: Confirmed by the printed continuation counterpart.

en: The messenger came and told it,
uncertainty_note: Confirmed by the printed continuation counterpart.

raw: Сени менен алышчу душман белен деп,
text: Сени менен алышчу душман белен деп,
en: Saying, “Was he an enemy fit to fight you?”
uncertainty_note: Confirmed by the printed continuation counterpart; the manuscript keeps деп on the same baseline.

en: Listen and speak, oh my people, as you go,
uncertainty_note: Very pale completion-first reading; элим and the final verb are especially uncertain.

en: He said to take Ala-Too and advance,
uncertainty_note: The verb phrase after Ала-Тоо is pale and provisional.

en: He had whetted them once again,
uncertainty_note: The final word appears to be the variant кайтадан.

en: Let him not retreat from the Kazakh without dying,
uncertainty_note: Completion-first reading; the first noun and final verb need later comparison.

en: You yourself prepared the arms and weapons,
uncertainty_note: The opening phrase and final verb are readable only provisionally.

en: Your fighting gaze was subdued,
uncertainty_note: The second half of the baseline is pale; көзүң басылган is provisional.

en: When was our rear ever at ease?
uncertainty_note: Completion-first reading; аркабыз жай болгон is clearer than the opening word.

en: A people said to bear a grieving fist,
uncertainty_note: Both the adjective and middle noun are uncertain completion-first readings.

en: Those people are the enemy who will fight,
uncertainty_note: The opening participle is pale but the rest of the line is clear.

en: Ala-Too is no land cheaply won,
uncertainty_note: Confirmed by the printed continuation counterpart.

en: They are not a people who will turn back,
uncertainty_note: Short pale baseline; the participle is provisional.

en: They say the ground is narrow for an attack,
uncertainty_note: The middle word is provisionally read зоолу and the idiom remains uncertain.

en: They say he is a mighty soul in battle,
uncertainty_note: The nouns are readable, but the exact construction is provisional.

en: To go without taking heed is an evil deed,
uncertainty_note: The first verb is pale and read provisionally as Бейлебей.

en: Unless we confront him and block his road,
uncertainty_note: Confirmed by the printed continuation counterpart.

en: Unless we scatter all he has gained,
uncertainty_note: Confirmed by the printed continuation counterpart.

en: Unless we surround and overrun his settlement,
uncertainty_note: Confirmed by the printed continuation counterpart; the handwriting is faint but consistent.

en: Slaughter the swift horses bred in Beijing,
uncertainty_note: Confirmed by the printed continuation counterpart.

en: This is one counsel spoken by your lord.
uncertainty_note: Confirmed by the printed continuation counterpart.

en: Braid the swift horses' manes,
uncertainty_note: Confirmed by the printed continuation counterpart.

en: Taking off your boots and stretching out your feet,
uncertainty_note: Confirmed by the printed continuation counterpart.

en: If you lie at ease, swelling with pride,
uncertainty_note: Confirmed by the printed continuation counterpart; Өрөпкөп is retained as printed.

en: Within five or six years,
uncertainty_note: Confirmed by the printed continuation counterpart.

en: The renowned grey-maned Kenen,
uncertainty_note: Confirmed by the printed continuation counterpart.

en: The infidel who has ravaged the people,
uncertainty_note: Confirmed by the printed continuation counterpart.

en: The fierce one, scourge of the age,
uncertainty_note: Confirmed by the printed continuation counterpart; translation follows the epithet's sense.

en: Rather than endure this lord,
uncertainty_note: The final verb is difficult; read as коргуча.

en: Would his spirit remain unsettled?
uncertainty_note: The middle word is read as жайрошпой; handwriting is faint.

en: Would he call it evil, would it strike him?
uncertainty_note: The second predicate is uncertain.

en: If he should raise and display his army,
uncertainty_note: Several letters in the opening phrase are ambiguous; completion-first reading.

en: If he gives it to the padishah and nothing remains,
uncertainty_note: The first word appears to be the dative form of кадыша.

en: Would he rest without putting up a fight?
Trembling at the khan’s command,
uncertainty_note: The last word may have a different initial consonant.

en: Would he stand without gathering an army?

raw: Бизде да кабары бар эми бар,
text: Бизде да кабары бар эми бар,
en: We too have word of it now,
uncertainty_note: The final two short words are crowded and uncertain.

en: If he takes an army from Hindustan,
If he breaks its pride at the very root,
uncertainty_note: The source wording is uncertain, especially Курактан and үзүп.

en: Countless hosts stand at his command,
uncertainty_note: Literal reading is uncertain; translated from the apparent sense.

en: His countless treasures are like a houseful,
uncertainty_note: The last word is uncertain.

en: His property is filled with yellow gold,
If there is a soul amid his worldly wealth,
uncertainty_note: The line is legible but its connection to the next line is uncertain.

en: Leave behind what remains,
uncertainty_note: The final word may be an inflected verbal form.

en: If the whole world were rich abundance,
uncertainty_note: The first two words are uncertain; completion-first interpretation.

en: If he were khan of a foreign people,
If there were a soul among that hearthful of people,
uncertainty_note: The middle wording is hard to resolve; translated cautiously.

en: Would he stand there without giving it thought?
Without bending his back and waist,
uncertainty_note: The opening word may instead be a personal name or body-part term.

en: Without taking a swift horse fit for him,
uncertainty_note: The middle word is uncertain.

en: He would not simply leave it while still unborn,
uncertainty_note: The opening verb and idiomatic sense are uncertain.

en: He would not appoint a weak man as beg,
Would not a heroic khan take his seat?
uncertainty_note: The verb may be конбойбу.

en: If there is a man in the saddle,
uncertainty_note: The manuscript looks like Ат ээринен; translated idiomatically.

en: If a man has but one doorway,
uncertainty_note: The last word and idiomatic sense are uncertain.

en: Would he not remain in the people’s place?
From the treasure of his in-laws’ people,
Would he not say, “I shall take my due”?
uncertainty_note: The adjective/adverb before аламын is uncertain.

en: Through the heart of that very land,
uncertainty_note: Several case endings are uncertain.

en: Would he not say, “I shall take the world”?
Contending against the Kongdai people,
uncertainty_note: The ethnonym and final verb are uncertain.

en: From my khan-father, blood-stained Manas.
The forty khans now rejoiced,
uncertainty_note: The middle word group is pale; кубаныган is a contextual reading.

en: At the news that had turned in their favor.
uncertainty_note: The first two words are difficult; English follows the apparent sense.

en: Each man made his speech brief,
uncertainty_note: The last word may be a closely related form.

en: The best of them spoke noble words,
uncertainty_note: Syntax is compressed and the last word is faint.

en: It was Khan Suurgulgan’s counsel.
uncertainty_note: The proper name is read as Суургулган; compare adjacent leaves.

en: Suurgulgan came forward and spoke,
uncertainty_note: The middle verb is faint but fits the visible letter forms.

en: What counsel did you see among them?
uncertainty_note: The opening noun is especially uncertain.

en: What you said of Suurgulgan,
uncertainty_note: The ending is pale; English is provisional.

en: Is the example of a tested young warrior,
uncertainty_note: The first word may be a related participial form.

en: Seeing Chyn Temir, I saw the people,
uncertainty_note: Proper name is clear; the repeated көр- forms are visually likely.

en: Cherish him and show him as an example,
uncertainty_note: Several letters are indistinct; translation follows the apparent imperative sense.

en: Suurgulgan set forth his thought,
uncertainty_note: Оюн тартып is legible but idiomatic force is uncertain.

en: When they heard Suurgulgan’s words,
uncertainty_note: Proper name spelling should be checked against adjacent leaves.

en: The armor-clad heroes,
uncertainty_note: The first word may name a particular kind of armor.

en: The heroes in coats of mail,
uncertainty_note: The manuscript ending is faint; normalized as баданалуу.

en: The gathered Kazaks formed a host,
uncertainty_note: The final word is uncertain though it resembles казактар.

en: The eloquent men in felt coats,
uncertainty_note: Both nouns are visually plausible; semantic pairing needs review.

en: The warriors who commanded thousands,
uncertainty_note: The final plural form is dialectal or uncertain.

en: Their ranks lay coiled like a snake,
uncertainty_note: The final noun is difficult; English follows visible түркүм-.

en: Here was the seething army,
uncertainty_note: Reading is comparatively clear.

en: When the khan’s command arrived,
uncertainty_note: Reading is comparatively clear.

en: They ran from the host toward the horde,
uncertainty_note: The case ending and топтон are faint.

en: The horde reeled and fell into turmoil,
uncertainty_note: The middle verb is highly uncertain.

en: Suurgulgan and Chyn Temir,
uncertainty_note: The two proper names are clear enough but spelling awaits comparison.

en: When the command to fight arrived,
uncertainty_note: The initial word could be another related verbal form.

en: They rushed like the men of Kemin,
uncertainty_note: The ethnonym or place-derived form is uncertain.

en: At dawn they bristled upright,
uncertainty_note: This line is difficult; raw reading and English are provisional.

en: Saying they would tirelessly persuade them with words,
uncertainty_note: The manuscript may omit or alter a suffix in көндүрүп.

en: The khans who formed a looming host,
uncertainty_note: The first word is uncertain but resembles караан.

en: Those fierce souls,
uncertainty_note: The first word is unclear and may be a different adjective.

en: Saying they would submit them to his command,
uncertainty_note: Reading is plausible but pale.

en: Its badly wearied old men,
uncertainty_note: The middle word is uncertain.

en: Every last one girded his waist.
uncertainty_note: The opening word is very uncertain and may continue or correct the preceding line.
